Theorem (Inclusion-Exclusion Principle for Finite Sets):
Let \(S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_n\) be finite sets. Then the size of their union is given by the inclusion-exclusion principle:
\[ |S_1 \cup S_2 \cup \cdots \cup S_n| = \sum_{i=1}^{n} |S_i| - \sum_{1 \leq i < j \leq n} |S_i \cap S_j| + \sum_{1 \leq i < j < k \leq n} |S_i \cap S_j \cap S_k| - \cdots + (-1)^{n+1} |S_1 \cap S_2 \cap \cdots \cap S_n| \]

fixes S :: "'a set list"
assumes "finite S"
shows "card (Union S) = (\<Sum>n ∈ {1..length S}::nat. card (set (nth S n)) - (\<Sum>i < j. card (set (nth S i) \<inter> set (nth S j))) + (\<Sum>i < j < k. card (set (nth S i) \<inter> set (nth S j) \<inter> set (nth S k))) - (\<Sum>i < j < k < l. card (set (nth S i) \<inter> set (nth S j) \<inter> set (nth S k) \<inter> set (nth S l))) + (-1)^(length S) * card (Inter S))"
